statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-58011 is an out-of-bounds read of up to 2 bytes in g_date_time_get_ymd (glib/gdatetime.c) when it processes an invalid GDateTime produced by g_date_time_add_full, which can corrupt date output or cause a denial of service. Upstream fixed it in GLib 2.86.5, 2.88.1 and 2.89.0 (https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/glib/-/issues/3917), and Debian backported the fix to trixie in 2.84.4-3~deb13u4 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-58011). This owner rebuilds Debian's trixie glib2.0 source. We unpacked libglib2.0-0t64 from every published build for amd64 and arm64. The three builds of Debian 2.84.4-3~deb13u3 do not carry the fix: their package changelog has no entry for this CVE. The three builds of Debian 2.84.4-3~deb13u5 do: their changelog includes the 2.84.4-3~deb13u4 entry that adds the patches from upstream 2.86.5 (the gdatetime range-validation patches) and names this CVE. The range ends at the first build of Debian 2.84.4-3~deb13u5, the first published build with the fix.
